request: Make SAGE fail-closed recovery self-directing and recurrence-aware so SAGE, not the LLM/operator, determines the next governed boundary from persisted failure identity, governing-condition lineage, and lifecycle authority.
required_capability: Deterministic recovery resolution with cross-attempt recurrence identity, consumed-governance-change lineage, loop prevention, accepted-control failure escalation, and exactly one repository-owned next operator boundary.

candidates_considered.insufficiency: Two identical request-execution failures at the same repository authority were each emitted with classification=new, recurrence.recurred=false, and no previous_failure_references.
The post-retrieval continuation decision repeatedly marks the same repository-owned-composition condition as changed and emits planning re-entry without durable consumed-change identity.
The parent lifecycle obeys planning re-entry but does not reject a second identical re-entry caused by an unchanged already-consumed governing change.
An accepted control that fails its live acceptance behavior has no repository-owned escalation that emits a successor gap/action and one next operator boundary.

gap.missing_interface_or_behavior: SAGE lacks a canonical persisted recovery identity/next-boundary contract. It cannot currently link identical failures across attempts, mark a governing change as consumed by the re-entry it caused, prevent duplicate re-entry, or escalate failure of an already-accepted control without LLM/operator inference.
gap.why_configuration_is_insufficient: The same failure repeated at the same branch, HEAD, upstream, remote-main observation, request, correction disposition, and planning boundary; runner or environment configuration cannot supply missing cross-attempt lineage.
gap.why_composition_is_insufficient: Existing primitives diagnose failures, retrieve evidence, classify governing changes, plan, execute, and manage action lifecycle, but their compositions do not share durable recovery identity and consumed-change semantics.

approval.rationale: The Architect explicitly directed 'make it so' after the live Action-002 sequence demonstrated that SAGE should provide the primitives/composition decision and tell the operator what to do rather than requiring source-code inspection and LLM-invented recovery.
